# useFullscreen

> Enter, exit and toggle full screen for an element, with live state and error capture.

🟡 intermediate · React 18.0+ · Custom Hooks › Browser & DOM · support: browser-limited

**Playground:** `npm run dev` → [`#/entry/use-fullscreen`](http://localhost:5173/#/entry/use-fullscreen)

## Concept

`isFullscreen` is derived from `document.fullscreenElement` through `useSyncExternalStore` (subscribed to `fullscreenchange` and `webkitfullscreenchange`). `enter`/`exit`/`toggle` call the standard API or its prefixed fallback and store failures in `error`.

## Problem

Local `isFullscreen` state goes stale when the user leaves with Esc or the browser UI; unhandled promise rejections appear when `requestFullscreen()` runs without a user gesture; prefix differences break older Safari.

## When to use

- Presentations, image/video viewers, games, dashboards on wall screens.

## When not to use

- Plain `<video>` — the native controls already include full screen.

## API

```ts
function useFullscreen<T extends Element = HTMLElement>(options?: {
  fullscreenOptions?: FullscreenOptions;
}): {
  ref: (node: T | null) => void;
  isFullscreen: boolean;
  isSupported: boolean;
  enter(): Promise<void>;
  exit(): Promise<void>;
  toggle(): Promise<void>;
  error: Error | null;
};
```

| Parameter                                | Type                | Description                                     |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `options.fullscreenOptions` _(optional)_ | `FullscreenOptions` | Passed to `requestFullscreen` (`navigationUI`). |

**Returns:** `{ ref, isFullscreen, isSupported, enter, exit, toggle, error }`. The promises never reject. Destructure the result (it contains `ref`).

## Common mistakes

### Requesting full screen without a gesture

❌ Incorrect:

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  void enter();
}, []);
```

Browsers require transient user activation; the request is rejected (`error` is set).

✅ Correct:

```tsx
<button onClick={() => void enter()}>Full screen</button>
```

## Edge cases

- `isFullscreen` is `false` when _another_ element is full screen.
- `exit()` is a no-op when nothing is full screen (the native call would reject).
- Controls rendered outside the element are not visible in full screen — put them inside.

## Browser support

Unprefixed in Chromium, Firefox and Safari 16.4+; older Safari uses the `webkit` prefix (handled). iPhone Safari only supports full screen for `<video>` (via `webkitEnterFullscreen`), so `isSupported` is `false` there. Iframes need `allow="fullscreen"`.
